answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds. Each agent locks real collateral before it earns or votes, and randomized audits pair agents to verify each other's work. A caught clone forfeits its bond to the honest challenger, so masquerading as a crowd requires posting a crowd of bonds. The attacker's cost grows linearly with every fake identity; the chance of an audit turns the whole stake into a liability. Neither an ivory credential, a botnet spread across the nebula, nor a reassuring fable changes that arithmetic.
